pr_title: [3.x] Fix error when having BoneAttachment before PhysicalBone
pr_body:
Fixes #42010

`bind_child_node_to_bone()` allows re-adding an existing bind. But `unbind_child_node_from_bone()` does not have extra checks for unbinding a non-existing bindings. So `List::erase()` complains about erasing something that does not exist.

There's no error when no `BoneAttachment` node comes before a `PhysicalBone`. This is because calling `List::erase()` on an empty list won't print an error. (Bone attachments are also bind to bones, so when there's a bone attachment node before the physical bone, the bind node list is not empty when it enters tree.)

It's inconsistent that `List::erase()` behaves differently when empty and non-empty. But I think fixing this on `Skeleton` level is acceptable since we prefer local solutions :stuck_out_tongue: 

There're no such methods on `master`.
pr_comments: Might be worth reviewing at the same time whether this should be a `List` at all versus a `LocalVector`. There's a whole bunch of stuff in Godot using `List`s that really should be `LocalVector`s (due to linked lists being so bad for cache etc). At some point it would be nice to go through these.

issue_context.title: Having BoneAttachment node before a Physical Bone for the same bone throws error
issue_context.body:
<!-- Please search existing issues for potential duplicates before filing yours:
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues?q=is%3Aissue
-->

**Godot version:** 3.2.2 stable
<!-- Specify commit hash if using non-official build. -->


**OS/device including version:** Windows 10
<!-- Specify GPU model, drivers, and the backend (GLES2, GLES3, Vulkan) if graphics-related. -->


**Issue description:**
<!-- What happened, and what was expected. -->

having a bone attachment node attached to a non root bone before a physical bone for that same bone in the heirarchy as shown:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/7292421/93003927-f0157f80-f4ff-11ea-9ddf-a1cff9312aba.png)

throws this error message:
 scene/3d/skeleton.cpp:637 - Condition "bones[p_bone].physical_bone" is true.
 ./core/list.h:158 - Condition "!p_I" is true. Returned: false
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/7292421/93003872-90b76f80-f4ff-11ea-9c99-69e666f19435.png)


and this error message when run:
E 0:00:00.501   erase: Condition "!p_I" is true. Returned: false
  <C++ Source>  ./core/list.h:158 @ erase()
everything works fine, but you get that error message for each bone on scene load 

But if you rearrange it this way it works fine with no error message:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/7292421/93003923-e8ee7180-f4ff-11ea-8844-ec857049eed1.png)


**Minimal reproduction project:**
<!-- A small Godot project which reproduces the issue. Drag and drop a zip archive to upload it. -->
[boneerrormessagedemonstration.zip](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/files/5213191/boneerrormessagedemonstration.zip)
project contains two scenes: HasErrorMessage.tscn and NoErrorMessage.tscn, which show it not working correctly and it working correctly respectively
comments:
I think attaching a BoneAttachment might actually un-parent the Physical Bones. I keep finding their collision shapes at the world origin.
![bones](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/10768827/94345898-b8720180-ffee-11ea-94fe-a505e955bfcd.png)

review_comments: Are the `nodes_bound` required to be in order? If not, we can maybe use `remove_unordered()`.. :thinking:

`Skeleton` itself does not require some specific order. But changing `nodes_bound` order affect the order of the returned array from `get_bound_child_nodes_to_bone()` and the `bound_children` property. So using `remove_unordered()` might break user code I think.
Can you store the element returned and use this to call `erase` using the element directly rather than by value?
